Appearance — themes, logo and favicon

Repaint the console with named themes built from the stylesheet's design tokens, and optionally replace the brand logo and favicon.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → User Interface → Appearance (URL /settings/#tab-appearance)

What is it?#

Appearance is the Settings pane where an administrator chooses how the SATOM console looks. A theme is a named set of overrides for the stylesheet's 34 design tokens (sidebar, top bar, surfaces, accent, brand gradients, text, status colours, shadows, layout sizes and font), plus an optional brand logo and favicon. One theme is active at a time and applies to every user, every ADOM and the sign-in pages.

What does it do?#

  • Ships four built-in themes: SATOM Aurora (the default look), SATOM Classic, SATOM Slate and SATOM Graphite. Built-ins cannot be edited or deleted.
  • Lets you create, edit, Duplicate, Apply, Export, import and Delete your own themes.
  • Import from a site… builds a theme from a website's brand colours, icon and favicon, or copies a theme (logo and favicon included) from another SATOM node.
  • Previews edits live on the page before anything is saved.
  • Audits text contrast (WCAG 2.1) and asks for confirmation before saving an unreadable palette.
  • Replaces the top-bar logo and the browser favicon while a theme that carries them is active.
  • Offers a one-click way back: Revert to the shipped look.

Requirements#

None. A fresh install already has the four built-ins, with SATOM Aurora active.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Every Appearance action requires users.manage (the Administrator profile). For other users the User Interface group, and with it the Appearance pane, is not rendered at all; the theme routes return 403 Forbidden if called directly.

The active theme's logo and favicon are served without a sign-in, because they also appear on the sign-in, forgot-password, reset-password and two-factor pages.

How to use#

Open Settings, then User Interface → Appearance. The pane has three cards: Themes (the list), Theme editor, and What a theme can and cannot repaint. Import from a site… in the Themes footer opens a fourth, Import from a site.

Switch to another theme#

  1. In Themes, find the theme. The active one carries an active badge and its name is shown next to Active: in the card header.
  2. Click Apply on its row. The flash message reads Theme '<name>' applied.

Every user sees the new look on their next page load (other server workers pick it up within about 15 seconds).

Create a theme from an existing one#

  1. Click Duplicate on the theme you want to start from. A copy named <name> copy is created, inactive. Flash: Theme '<copy>' created from '<name>' — edit it below.
  2. Click Edit on the copy. The Theme editor loads its values and shows Editing: <name>.
  3. Change any token. Each field shows the stylesheet default; colour tokens also have a colour picker, gradient tokens a preview strip, and the ↻ button puts a field back to the stylesheet default.
  4. As you type, the page previews the change and the server validates it. Invalid values appear in a red box; contrast findings appear in a Contrast box.
  5. Optionally upload a Brand logo and/or Favicon, or tick remove current to drop an existing one.
  6. Click Save theme. Flash: Theme '<name>' saved.
  7. Click Apply on the row to make it the console theme.

💡Tip

Saving a theme does not activate it. Editing a theme that is not active changes nothing for anyone until you click Apply.

Create a theme from scratch#

  1. Click New theme in the editor footer (this also stops any preview).
  2. Enter Theme name (required, unique) and, optionally, Description.
  3. Change the tokens you want and click Save theme. Flash: Theme '<name>' created.

Stop a preview#

The live preview applies only to the page you are on and is discarded when you navigate away. Click Stop preview to return the page to the active theme without leaving it.

Export and import a theme#

  1. Click Export on any theme row, built-ins included. A file named satom-theme-<slug>.json is downloaded.
  2. On the target install, choose the file next to Import theme in the Themes card footer and click Import theme. Flash: Theme '<name>' imported with its logo and favicon. (or just imported. when the theme has neither). The imported theme is inactive. If a theme with that name already exists, the import is named <name> (imported), then <name> (imported 2), <name> (imported 3) and so on, so the same file can be imported any number of times.

The file holds the theme name, description, token overrides, logo and favicon (schema satom.ui-theme/2). Files exported by older versions (schema satom.ui-theme/1) hold no logo or favicon and still import.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: importing the same theme file a third time no longer fails, and the logo and favicon pickers offer every format the server accepts.

Copy a theme from another SATOM node#

  1. On the node that has the theme, create an API token with the read scope (API Tokens, see API tokens) and copy it.
  2. On this node, click Import from a site… in the Themes footer.
  3. Under Another SATOM node, enter the Node address (for example https://satom-b.example.com), paste the token in API token from that node, and optionally a Theme name. Leave it empty for that node's active theme.
  4. Click Copy theme. Flash: Theme '<name> (from <node>)' copied from <node> with its logo and favicon. It is not applied yet: review it, then Apply.
  5. Click Edit to check it, then Apply.

The token is used for that one request and is not stored.

Build a theme from a website#

  1. Click Import from a site… in the Themes footer.
  2. Under Website, enter the Site address (www.example.com or a full URL) and click Build theme.
  3. A new theme named <site> (from <host>) is created, inactive, and one message per decision says where each value came from. For example: Brand colour #DA291C, from the most used colour in its stylesheets. and Logo: https://…/apple-touch-icon.png (its apple-touch-icon).
  4. Click Edit to preview it and adjust anything, then Apply.

What is taken, and from where:

Theme part Taken from
Accent, sidebar, top bar, brand gradients, glows The brand colour: the page's theme-color, else a brand-named CSS variable (--primary, --brand-*, --accent…), else the most used saturated colour
Sidebar active marker, accent gradient A second colour of a different hue, when the site has one
Sidebar background A dark background on a header, nav or sidebar rule, when there is one
Logo The site's apple-touch-icon, else its largest icon, else a header logo image no wider than 1.6:1
Favicon Its icon link closest to 64 px, else /favicon.ico

Every colour pair the contrast audit checks is kept at 4.5:1 or better; if the site's colour is too light for links on white, the accent is darkened and the report says so. The layout, page background, text colours, status colours and font are not taken.

ℹ️Note

The top-bar logo is a 28 × 28 px square, so a wide wordmark is skipped (the report says too wide for the square top-bar mark). Upload the logo you want in the editor afterwards if the site's icon is not it.

❗Important

This node fetches the page, its stylesheets and images itself, so it needs a route to the site (and to the internet for a public site). Internal sites are allowed. Loopback, link-local (including cloud metadata), multicast and reserved addresses are refused, and so is a URL with credentials in it.

Delete a theme#

Click Delete on a non-built-in theme and confirm the browser prompt. If it was the active theme, SATOM Aurora becomes active automatically.

Get back to the shipped look#

Click Revert to the shipped look in the Themes card footer. Flash: Reverted to 'SATOM Aurora'. If the console is too unreadable to use, see Troubleshooting.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Theme name Unique name, up to 128 characters. Yes Corporate blue
Description Free text, up to 300 characters. No Brand colours 2026
Brand logo Replaces the SATOM mark in the top bar (every ADOM) and on the sign-in page. PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF, ICO or SVG. No logo.svg
Favicon Browser tab icon. PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF, ICO or SVG. No favicon.png
Token fields One per design token, grouped Sidebar, Top bar, Surfaces, Accent, Brand, Text, Status, Elevation, Layout, Typography. Leave at the default to inherit the stylesheet. No #4F46E5
apply anyway (low contrast) Confirms saving a palette whose text contrast falls below 3.0:1. Shown when the contrast check reports an unreadable pair. When prompted ticked

Accepted token values by kind

Kind Used by Accepted form Example
color most tokens #rgb, #rgba, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa, rgb() / rgba() with numbers rgba(79, 70, 229, 0.10)
gradient Brand gradient, Accent gradient linear-gradient(...) or radial-gradient(...), optional direction, 2–8 colour stops linear-gradient(135deg, #0F172A 0%, #4F46E5 100%)
ratio Glow strength 0, 1 or a fraction with up to 3 decimals 0.2
length Sidebar width, Top bar height, corner radii 0 or a number with px, rem, em, %, vh, vw, ch 264px
shadow Card shadows none or offsets/blur/spread plus a colour 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)
transition Transition <time> <easing> 0.2s ease
font Font stack family names separated by commas 'Inter', Arial, sans-serif

Every value is also refused if it is longer than 240 characters or contains any of ; { } < > \ /* */ url( expression( @import javascript: or a line break.

Example#

🧪Example — Rebranding the console for a managed-service customer

  1. Duplicate SATOM Slate and Edit the copy; name it Customer A.
  2. Set Accent to #0B6E4F, Accent (hover) to #085A40 and Sidebar → Background to #12332A.
  3. Because a theme that leaves the gradients alone inherits the shipped blue ramp, also set Brand gradient to linear-gradient(135deg, #12332A 0%, #0B6E4F 60%, #3FB68B 100%).
  4. Upload the customer's SVG logo as Brand logo.
  5. Watch the Contrast box; it lists any text/background pair under 4.5:1.
  6. Save theme, then Apply.
  7. On the customer's second install, use Import from a site… → Another SATOM node (or Export here and Import theme there). The logo and favicon travel with the theme.

Result#

  • The active theme's overrides are emitted as a small stylesheet block on every page, including the sign-in pages; tokens you did not change keep following the shipped stylesheet.
  • The Overrides column shows how many of the 34 tokens a theme changes.
  • Each change is written to the audit log as settings.theme.create, .update, .duplicate, .activate, .delete, .import, .import_node, .import_site or .reset. The two last ones record the node or site host, never the token.

Troubleshooting#

"This palette drops text contrast below 3.0:1 in places — tick "apply anyway" to confirm."#

Possible causes - A text token (e.g. Primary text, Sidebar → Text, Accent) is too close in luminance to the surface it sits on.

Solution 1. Read the Contrast box: it names each pair and its ratio. 2. Adjust the colours, or tick apply anyway (low contrast) if the low contrast is intended, then Save theme again.

Verification - The flash shows Theme '<name>' saved. (or created.).

"<Token>: '<value>' is not a valid <kind> value"#

Possible causes - The value does not match the accepted form for that token's kind, e.g. a colour name such as red, a hsl() colour, or a gradient with a single stop.

Solution 1. Use one of the forms in Configuration, or click ↻ to restore the default.

Verification - The red error box in the editor disappears.

"Built-in themes cannot be edited — duplicate it first."#

Possible causes - You tried to save changes onto SATOM Aurora, Classic, Slate or Graphite.

Solution 1. Click Duplicate on the built-in, then Edit the copy.

Verification - The editor header reads Editing: <name> copy and saving succeeds.

"A theme named '<name>' already exists."#

Possible causes - Theme names must be unique.

Solution 1. Choose another Theme name (or, for Duplicate, rename the existing copy first).

"Import rejected — Not a SATOM theme (expected schema satom.ui-theme/2 or satom.ui-theme/1)." or "Import rejected — …"#

Possible causes - The file is not a SATOM theme export, one of its token values fails validation, or its logo or favicon is not a readable image. The whole file is refused; nothing is imported.

Solution 1. Fix or remove the named tokens (or the asset) in the JSON file and import again.

"Could not fetch the theme: TLS verification failed for <node>…"#

Possible causes - The other node's certificate is issued by a private CA this node does not trust.

Solution 1. Add that CA under Settings → Certificates & Trust → Trust store, then Copy theme again. Verification is never switched off.

"Could not fetch the theme: The other node refused: …" or "…did not answer with JSON…"#

Possible causes - The token is wrong, revoked or expired (Token is unknown, revoked, expired or malformed.), its owner is disabled, or no theme has the name given (No theme named …). - The other node runs a version without the theme endpoint, or the address points at something that is not a SATOM node.

Solution 1. Create a fresh read token on the other node and check the Theme name (it must match exactly), or leave it empty for the active theme. 2. Update the other node if it predates the endpoint.

"Could not read the site: <host> resolves to <address>, a loopback address…" (or link-local, multicast, reserved)#

Possible causes - The name resolves to an address this node never fetches from.

Solution 1. Use the site's public or internal (RFC 1918) address instead.

"Could not read the site: Could not reach <host>…" or "…did not answer within 10 s."#

Possible causes - This node has no route to the site, or the site is down or slow.

Solution 1. Check the node's outbound access to that host, or import from another node that can reach it and copy the theme across.

"Nothing usable found on <host>: no brand colour, icon or favicon."#

Possible causes - The site styles itself from script, is monochrome, and publishes no icons.

Solution 1. Build the theme by hand in the editor: Accent and Sidebar → Background carry most of a brand.

"Unsupported logo type (use PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF, ICO or SVG)." / "SVG too large (max 512 KB)." / "Image could not be processed: …"#

Possible causes - The upload has an unsupported extension, an SVG is over 512 KB, or a raster file is not a readable image.

Solution 1. Export the logo as PNG or a smaller SVG and upload again.

The console is unreadable and I cannot reach the Appearance pane#

Solution 1. If you can still click: Settings → User Interface → Appearance → Revert to the shipped look, or Apply on any built-in theme. 2. Otherwise, on the SATOM node as root run: satom execute reset theme It activates SATOM Aurora (see CLI).

Verification - After a reload the console shows the default blue/gold look and Active: reads SATOM Aurora.

I want a dark theme#

There is no supported dark theme. Status badges and some decorative tints still use fixed colours in the stylesheet, so a dark page background would leave those elements light. Light-background palettes are fully supported.

Advanced#

Advanced How themes are stored and applied
  • Themes live in the ui_themes table. A row stores only the tokens that differ from the stylesheet default; a value equal to the default is dropped when saving.
  • Exactly one row is active. Activation clears the flag on all rows and sets it on one; if no row is active, SATOM Aurora is used.
  • The active theme is cached per server worker for 15 seconds.
  • The token list is generated from the stylesheet, so the editor always offers every token the stylesheet exposes.
  • Values are validated again every time the CSS is emitted, not only when they are saved, so a row restored from a backup or edited directly in the database cannot inject CSS.
  • Built-in themes are re-synchronised with the shipped definition at every start; custom themes are never modified by an upgrade.
  • If loading the theme fails for any reason, pages render with the shipped stylesheet rather than failing.
Advanced Logo and favicon files
  • Uploads are stored under data/branding/ as theme-<id>-logo.* / theme-<id>-favicon.*. The data/ directory is replicated to the HA standby (see High availability), so the files follow a failover.
  • The theme rows are in the database and data/branding/ travels in the same system backup bundle; a restore puts the files back next to the rows. A bundle made before branding travelled has no such folder: after restoring one onto a rebuilt node, upload the logo and favicon again (edit the theme, choose the files, Save theme).
  • SVG uploads are sanitised (script, foreignObject, iframe, embed, object, event handlers in any quoting, javascript: and external links removed) and served with a sandbox Content-Security-Policy, so an SVG opened directly cannot run anything. Raster uploads are re-encoded as PNG and shrunk to fit 256 × 256 px. The top bar shows the mark at 28 × 28 px without stretching it.
  • With no theme logo, the top bar shows the SATOM emblem — not the per-ADOM mark. The per-ADOM marks set in Settings → ADOMs appear in the ADOM switcher and ADOM lists.
  • /favicon.ico redirects to the active theme's favicon when there is one.
  • Duplicate copies tokens only; the logo and favicon stay with the original theme. Import theme (a v2 file), Copy theme and Build theme bring a logo and favicon with them.
Advanced Contrast audit

Each text token is paired with the surface it is drawn on. Pairs under 4.5:1 (WCAG AA for body text) are reported as below AA 4.5:1; pairs under 3.0:1, or colours the auditor cannot parse, are reported as unreadable and require apply anyway (low contrast). Gradient tokens have no contrast partner and are not audited.
